% Appendix: Post-hoc Type Consistency Resolution (TCR)
% exp_ids: d065_tcr_pilot (all 10 configs)

\section{Post-hoc Type Consistency Resolution}
\label{app:tcr}

S1 enforces domain/range constraints per-triple but does not enforce global entity type consensus, leaving residual CF violations where the same entity receives different types across triples.
We evaluate a post-hoc resolution step (TCR): for each entity with conflicting type assignments, TCR selects the type that maximizes satisfaction count across all relations referencing that entity, subject to domain/range constraints.
Unlike naive majority voting (which ignores relational constraints and increases DR), TCR is constraint-aware: candidate types are scored by how many of the entity's relational contexts they satisfy.
TCR runs after S1 decoding completes and has access to the full document context.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: TCR results on SciERC
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.2pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll rr rr r r@{}}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CF (\%)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{DR (\%)}} & \textbf{$\Delta$E-F1} & \textbf{Fund.} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-7} \cmidrule(l){8-8}
\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & Pre & Post & Pre & Post & (pp) & (\%) \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Zero-shot}
  & Qwen    & 9.75 & \textbf{0} & 0.93  & 1.21  & $-$1.29 & 2.04 \\
  & Llama   & 6.40 & \textbf{0} & 0.08  & 0.30  & $-$1.78 & 1.85 \\
  & Mistral & 0.67 & \textbf{0} & 13.36 & 12.87 & $+$0.05 & 0 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{LoRA}
  & Qwen    & 1.19 & \textbf{0} & 0     & 0     & $-$0.75 & 0 \\
  & Llama   & 0.46 & \textbf{0} & 0.09  & 0.09  & $-$0.18 & 0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{TCR on SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$, 551 docs).
Pre/Post: before/after TCR.
$\Delta$E-F1: entity F1 change (F1$\times$100).
Fund.: percentage of conflicting entities where no single type satisfies all relational constraints (fundamental conflicts).
TCR eliminates all CF with DR increases $\leq$0.28\,pp; fundamental conflicts are 0--2\%.}
\label{tab:tcr-scierc}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: TCR results on DocRED
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.2pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll rr rr r r@{}}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CF (\%)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{DR (\%)}} & \textbf{$\Delta$E-F1} & \textbf{Fund.} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-7} \cmidrule(l){8-8}
\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & Pre & Post & Pre & Post & (pp) & (\%) \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Zero-shot}
  & Qwen    & 13.11 & \textbf{0} & 10.21 & 11.74 & $-$3.44 & 13.52 \\
  & Llama   & 23.71 & \textbf{0} &  2.55 & 11.93 & $-$5.21 & 22.78 \\
  & 70B     & 11.61 & \textbf{0} &  0    &  4.20 & $-$5.98 & 18.26 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{LoRA}
  & Qwen    &  0.42 & \textbf{0} &  0.01 &  0.14 & $-$0.16 & 12.16 \\
  & Llama   &  0.36 & \textbf{0} &  0.21 &  0.20 & $-$0.17 & 11.59 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{TCR on DocRED ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$, 998 docs).
Under zero-shot, TCR introduces substantial DR regressions (up to $+$9.38\,pp for Llama) and E-F1 drops (up to $-$5.98\,pp for 70B).
Fundamental conflict rates are 12--23\%, an order of magnitude higher than SciERC.
Under LoRA, low baseline CF (0.36--0.42\%) limits both TCR impact and DR cost.}
\label{tab:tcr-docred}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Analysis.}
TCR effectiveness correlates inversely with schema constraint tightness $\bar{\kappa}$.
On SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$), fundamental conflicts constitute 0--2\% of type disagreements: most conflicts are resolvable because the loose schema admits many valid type pairs, and TCR can find a type satisfying all relational contexts.
DR increases are bounded ($\leq$0.28\,pp), and E-F1 cost is modest ($\leq$1.78\,pp in zero-shot, $\leq$0.75\,pp under LoRA).
On DocRED ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$), 13--23\% of conflicts are fundamental: the tight schema renders most type pairs invalid, so unifying an entity's type across all its relational contexts inevitably violates some domain/range constraints.
This produces severe DR regressions under zero-shot (Llama: 2.55\%$\to$11.93\%; 70B: 0\%$\to$4.20\%), where baseline CF is high enough that many entities require resolution.
Under LoRA, baseline CF is already low (0.36--0.42\%), limiting both the scope for TCR improvement and the DR cost.

This $\bar{\kappa}$-dependent boundary is consistent with the constraint tightness analysis in \S\ref{sec:composition}: $\bar{\kappa}$ predicts not only decoding-time DR residual rates but also the feasibility of post-hoc type resolution.
Beam search (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}) resolves CF and DR simultaneously across all $\bar{\kappa}$ values (SciERC and DocRED 50-doc subset: DR$\to$0\% for calibrated models), making it the preferred approach for high-tightness schemas.
TCR is a zero-cost complement for low-tightness schemas where beam search latency (1.54$\times$) is undesirable.

% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion
% Full discussion in Appendix; Mistral boundary condition in app:dual-factor.

OntoCoDec compiles IE schemas into composable token-level constraints: LoRA + greedy S1 achieves DR\,$\leq$\,0.20\% with CF\,$\leq$\,1.2\%; beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violations on SciERC (R-F1 44--46, 1.54$\times$ latency); zero-shot DR drops 42--99\% across four models (8B--70B).
Post-hoc type resolution complements S1 on low-$\bar{\kappa}$ schemas (Appendix~\ref{app:tcr}); global type consensus and GoLLIE-style schema encoding are future work.

% Appendix: Post-hoc Type Consistency Resolution (TCR)
% exp_ids: d065_tcr_pilot (all 10 configs)

\section{Post-hoc Type Consistency Resolution}
\label{app:tcr}

S1 enforces domain/range constraints per-triple but does not enforce global entity type consensus, leaving residual CF violations where the same entity receives different types across triples.
We evaluate a post-hoc resolution step (TCR): for each entity with conflicting type assignments, TCR selects the type that maximizes satisfaction count across all relations referencing that entity, subject to domain/range constraints.
Unlike naive majority voting (which ignores relational constraints and increases DR), TCR is constraint-aware: candidate types are scored by how many of the entity's relational contexts they satisfy.
TCR runs after S1 decoding completes and has access to the full document context.

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: TCR results on SciERC
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.2pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll rr rr r r@{}}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CF (\%)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{DR (\%)}} & \textbf{$\Delta$E-F1} & \textbf{Fund.} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-7} \cmidrule(l){8-8}
\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & Pre & Post & Pre & Post & (pp) & (\%) \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Zero-shot}
  & Qwen    & 9.75 & \textbf{0} & 0.93  & 1.21  & $-$1.29 & 2.04 \\
  & Llama   & 6.40 & \textbf{0} & 0.08  & 0.30  & $-$1.78 & 1.85 \\
  & Mistral & 0.67 & \textbf{0} & 13.36 & 12.87 & $+$0.05 & 0 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{LoRA}
  & Qwen    & 1.19 & \textbf{0} & 0     & 0     & $-$0.75 & 0 \\
  & Llama   & 0.46 & \textbf{0} & 0.09  & 0.09  & $-$0.18 & 0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{TCR on SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$, 551 docs).
Pre/Post: before/after TCR.
$\Delta$E-F1: entity F1 change (F1$\times$100).
Fund.: percentage of conflicting entities where no single type satisfies all relational constraints (fundamental conflicts).
TCR eliminates all CF with DR increases $\leq$0.28\,pp; fundamental conflicts are 0--2\%.}
\label{tab:tcr-scierc}
\end{table}

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: TCR results on DocRED
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.2pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll rr rr r r@{}}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CF (\%)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{DR (\%)}} & \textbf{$\Delta$E-F1} & \textbf{Fund.} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-7} \cmidrule(l){8-8}
\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & Pre & Post & Pre & Post & (pp) & (\%) \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Zero-shot}
  & Qwen    & 13.11 & \textbf{0} & 10.21 & 11.74 & $-$3.44 & 13.52 \\
  & Llama   & 23.71 & \textbf{0} &  2.55 & 11.93 & $-$5.21 & 22.78 \\
  & 70B     & 11.61 & \textbf{0} &  0    &  4.20 & $-$5.98 & 18.26 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{LoRA}
  & Qwen    &  0.42 & \textbf{0} &  0.01 &  0.14 & $-$0.16 & 12.16 \\
  & Llama   &  0.36 & \textbf{0} &  0.21 &  0.20 & $-$0.17 & 11.59 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{TCR on DocRED ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$, 998 docs).
Under zero-shot, TCR introduces substantial DR regressions (up to $+$9.38\,pp for Llama) and E-F1 drops (up to $-$5.98\,pp for 70B).
Fundamental conflict rates are 12--23\%, an order of magnitude higher than SciERC.
Under LoRA, low baseline CF (0.36--0.42\%) limits both TCR impact and DR cost.}
\label{tab:tcr-docred}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Analysis.}
TCR effectiveness correlates inversely with schema constraint tightness $\bar{\kappa}$.
On SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$), fundamental conflicts constitute 0--2\% of type disagreements: most conflicts are resolvable because the loose schema admits many valid type pairs, and TCR can find a type satisfying all relational contexts.
DR increases are bounded ($\leq$0.28\,pp), and E-F1 cost is modest ($\leq$1.78\,pp in zero-shot, $\leq$0.75\,pp under LoRA).
On DocRED ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$), 13--23\% of conflicts are fundamental: the tight schema renders most type pairs invalid, so unifying an entity's type across all its relational contexts inevitably violates some domain/range constraints.
This produces severe DR regressions under zero-shot (Llama: 2.55\%$\to$11.93\%; 70B: 0\%$\to$4.20\%), where baseline CF is high enough that many entities require resolution.
Under LoRA, baseline CF is already low (0.36--0.42\%), limiting both the scope for TCR improvement and the DR cost.

This $\bar{\kappa}$-dependent boundary is consistent with the constraint tightness analysis in \S\ref{sec:composition}: $\bar{\kappa}$ predicts not only decoding-time DR residual rates but also the feasibility of post-hoc type resolution.
Beam search (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}) resolves CF and DR simultaneously across all $\bar{\kappa}$ values (SciERC and DocRED 50-doc subset: DR$\to$0\% for calibrated models), making it the preferred approach for high-tightness schemas.
TCR is a zero-cost complement for low-tightness schemas where beam search latency (1.54$\times$) is undesirable.

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_unconstrained, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}
Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET ($\to$\,0\%), and near-eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%).\footnote{The residual 0.03\% RV traces to a rare XGrammar automaton edge case where subword tokens from different enum entries combine into chimeric values (e.g., \texttt{member} + \texttt{icipant\_of} from \texttt{member\_of} and \texttt{participant\_of}). This is not a fundamental limitation of the approach.}
R-F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; $p < 0.001$), attributable to elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions.
CF increases modestly (0.10\%\,$\to$\,2.57\%), consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only, phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
\paragraph{Layer contributions.}
Grammar-only eliminates RV and ET but \emph{increases} DR to 26.17\%: OOV triples (29.66\% baseline) become evaluable and expose latent type incompatibilities.\footnote{The grammar-only DR increase reflects constraint-altered generation trajectories in long documents, where vocabulary restriction shifts token probabilities away from natural but type-violating sequences.}
Semantic-only reduces DR by 25\% but cannot eliminate RV or ET, the same enabling dependency observed on SciERC.
Residual DR (10.21\% vs.\ SciERC's 0.93\%) reflects higher tightness ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$ vs.\ 0.333), which forces frequent fallback; effective semantic coverage is $\sim$90\% (Appendix~\ref{app:fallback-coverage}).
Under fine-tuning, residual narrows to 0.01--0.20\% (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).
The increase in Llama parse failures under constraints (6.8\%\,$\to$\,9.1\%) reflects an inherent trade-off: constraint masking alters token probability distributions, which can push generation toward suboptimal paths in long documents.
